title: TEN-DM: Topology-Enhanced Diffusion Model for Spatio-Temporal Event Prediction
claim: Heterogeneous views of raw event data are encoded in parallel and fused by topology-guided attention to condition a diffusion model.
layout: 3 numbered panels, left-to-right, color-coded input arrows into fusion block
description: A three-stage left-to-right figure with numbered black circles. Stage 1 is a large real map of Philadelphia with red dots marking events. A black arrow leads to stage 2, a boxed column of four color-tinted input views: a temporal stem plot on a timeline, a spatial scatter plot with latitude and longitude axes, a time-series image strip of four daypart maps (00:00–05:59 to 18:00–23:59), and a graph of nodes and edges. Colored arrows (blue, green, orange, purple) point from each view to stage 3. Stage 3 holds rotated labeled boxes for Temporal Encoding, Spatial Encoding, TLL and GNN. The first three feed a gray TST-MHA block, which feeds a tall pink Diffusion Model bar. The GNN output goes directly to the diffusion bar. The eye goes first to the red-dotted map.
caption: Overview of the TEN-DM model: (1) a sequence of events; (2) extracted temporal, spatial, time-series image, and graph information; (3) key components including temporal encoding, spatial encoding, temporal topological learning module (TLL), graph representation learning (GNN), and topology-guided spatio-temporal multi-head attention (TST-MHA).
abstract: Spatio-temporal point process (STPP) data appear in many domains. A natural way to model them is to describe how the instantaneous event rate varies over space and time given the observed history which enables interpretation, interaction detection, and forecasting. Traditional parametric kernel-based models, while historically dominant, struggle to capture complex nonlinear patterns. In contrast, deep learning methods leverage the representational power of neural networks to aggregate historical events and integrate spatio-temporal point processes. However, existing deep learning methods often process space and time independently, overlooking the spatio-temporal dependencies. To address this limitation, we propose a novel method called Topology-ENhanced Diffusion Model (TEN-DM), including two key components namely spatio-temporal graph construction and multimodal topological feature representation learning. Further, we use temporal query technique to effectively capture periodic temporal patterns for learning effective temporal representations. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of TEN-DM on multiple STPP datasets compared to state-of-the-art methods.
